chunk_findings.detail: The module promises (docstring, and the stated acceptance for D-upstream-reporting) that "gh missing **or not logged in** is `Unavailable` with the reason", but `_ask` only maps `ForgeUnavailable` to `Unavailable`; every non-zero `gh` exit becomes `GhError`. Running `ensure_ready` with `gh` installed but unauthenticated invokes `gh auth status`, which exits non-zero with "You are not logged into any GitHub hosts"; `_check` raises `ForgeError` for a command that ran and failed, and `_ask` therefore raises `GhError`, not `Unavailable`. The same happens on the send path: `create_issue` on an unauthenticated machine gets `GhError` from `gh issue create`. Consequence: the "not logged in" state is indistinguishable from any other gh failure, so a caller that (per the spec) treats `Unavailable` as the "UNAVAILABLE with the reason, never silent" outcome will surface a raw/redacted error or crash instead of reporting the unavailable reason. Concrete demo: `ensure_ready(tmp_path, runner=runner_that_exits_1_with_auth_status_message)` raises `GhError`, contradicting both the module's own docstring and the acceptance criterion.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/upstream_gh.py:38-44 (`_ask` / `ensure_ready`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The module's stated security invariant — the docstring says the consent is "MINTED elsewhere (the operator's interactive yes ...); nothing in this module can create one" — is not enforced by the code. `send_gh` performs its gate solely through attribute reads and a `consume()` call on a duck-typed object (`_refusal` does `getattr(consent, "digest"/"used"/"expires_at")`, then `consent.consume()`), and the `Consent` dataclass that satisfies all three is defined right here with a public constructor. So the "agent-supplied flag alone is refused" test passes only for the trivial flag case, while a slightly richer input bypasses it entirely. Given the bundle's known digest (it is printed in `Outcome.digest`, used as the file name under `.ddflow/local/reports/<digest>.md`, and embedded in the preview URL), an agent can call

    upstream_delivery.send_gh(root, bundle, "owner/name",
                              upstream_delivery.Consent(bundle.digest, time.time() + 3600))

— or equivalently `SimpleNamespace(digest=bundle.digest, expires_at=1e18, used=False, consume=lambda: True)` — and `_refusal` returns "", `consent.consume()` returns True, and `gh.create_issue` is invoked, i.e. an upstream issue is submitted with no operator consent. The gate therefore verifies the *shape* of the consent, not its authenticity: there is no signature, nonce, or minter-only handle, so any in-process caller that can read the digest (which the module itself licenses) can mint a valid consent. To match the stated invariant, the send path must depend on a value that only the trusted minter can produce (e.g. a token/signature checked against a minter-held secret), rather than accepting any object exposing `digest`/`expires_at`/`used`/`consume`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upstream_delivery.py:88 (`Consent` / `send_gh`)

chunk_findings.detail: The corpus for the acceptance test is derived from the repository's own runtime state, `EVENTS = ROOT / ".ddflow" / "events"`, i.e. `ROOT/.ddflow/events/*.jsonl`, which is mutable, machine-local log data. Nothing in this file (or any fixture) creates that directory or seeds it with events. On a clean clone or CI runner where `.ddflow/events` does not exist, `EVENTS.glob("*.jsonl")` yields an empty iterator, `_real_bug_texts()` returns `[]`, and the hard assertion `assert len(texts) > 50` raises `AssertionError` before a single URL is measured — so the acceptance test ("URL < 8 KB for the whole real-text corpus") fails unconditionally in that environment, and on a developer machine it passes or fails based on unrelated local logs. The same test is also sensitive to the log contents it is fed: `_real_bug_texts()` appends `str((e.get("data") or {}).get("summary", ""))` without filtering, so any `bug.found` event without a `data.summary` contributes `""`, and `_bundle(title=t[:100], expected=t, ...)` is then invoked with an empty title/expected, which is not a case this test was written to exercise. The test needs a committed/static corpus (or a fixture that writes one into `tmp_path`) rather than reading the live `.ddflow/events` log.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_upstream_delivery.py: `_real_bug_texts` / `test_url_under_8kb_for_the_whole_real_text_corpus`

chunk_findings.detail: `ensure_ready` relies on `_ask(runner, cwd, ["gh", "auth", "status"], ...)` to classify "not logged in" as `Unavailable`, but `gh auth status` exits with a **non-zero status code** when no host is authenticated (it prints "You are not logged into any GitHub hosts…" and returns 1). Given `_ask`'s own structure — it catches `ForgeUnavailable` (process could not be asked, e.g. missing binary) separately from `ForgeError` (the tool ran and said no) — a non-zero exit from an installed `gh` produces `ForgeError`, which `_ask` converts to `GhError`, not `Unavailable`. So in the exact environment the acceptance criteria call out ("gh missing or not logged in is UNAVAILABLE with the reason"), `ensure_ready` raises `GhError`. The caller/dispatcher that branches on `Unavailable` vs `GhError` will therefore report the not-logged-in case under the wrong outcome (treated as a sent-and-rejected `gh` error rather than an unavailable precondition), contradicting both the module docstring ("`gh` missing or not logged in is `Unavailable` with the reason") and the stated behavior. Demonstrate: put a logged-out `gh` on `PATH`, call `ensure_ready(cwd)`; `gh auth status` returns exit 1 → `ForgeError` → `_ask` raises `GhError`, whereas the spec requires `Unavailable` carrying the reason.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/upstream_gh.py:38 (`ensure_ready`)

chunk_findings.detail: The consent gate is bypassable by any caller, including the agent it is supposed to bind. `Consent` is a plain public dataclass in this very module with an unguarded constructor, and `send_gh` validates consent purely structurally (`_refusal` only `getattr`s `digest`/`used`/`expires_at`). So the "agent-supplied flag alone is refused" test only covers the `True`/bool case (which fails because a bool has no `digest`); it does not cover a forged `Consent`. Concretely, `send_gh(root, bundle, "owner/repo", Consent(digest=bundle.digest, expires_at=time.time() + 3600))` passes `_refusal` (digest matches, `used` is False, not expired), `consent.consume()` returns True, and `gh.create_issue(...)` is invoked — the agent has minted its own approval and the operator never said yes. This directly contradicts the module docstring ("The consent object is DEFINED here and MINTED elsewhere ... nothing in this module can create one") and defeats the stated intent that sending "requires a `Consent` whose digest equals the digest of the exact bytes being sent" and can only be granted by the operator's interactive yes. The `ConsentLike` runtime-checkable Protocol does not help, since `_refusal` uses duck-typed `getattr` and never verifies that the object originated from the trusted minter.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upstream_delivery.py — `Consent` / `send_gh`

chunk_findings.detail: The module docstring, the acceptance criteria, and the linked decision all require "not logged in" to surface as `Unavailable` with the reason. `ensure_ready` calls `_ask`, which only produces `Unavailable` when the runner raises `ForgeUnavailable` (i.e. the binary is missing/`FileNotFoundError`); a non-zero exit is translated to `ForgeError` and re-raised as `GhError`. `gh auth status` prints its "not logged into any GitHub hosts" diagnostics and exits **1** in exactly the logged-out environment this function is supposed to classify. So in the environment "gh installed but not authenticated", `ensure_ready` raises `GhError`, not `Unavailable`. Any caller that gates on the `Unavailable` type (e.g. `services/upstream_delivery` mapping it to the UNAVAILABLE delivery status) will instead take the hard-error path, contradicting "gh missing or not logged in is UNAVAILABLE with the reason". Suggest discriminating on the auth-status return code/message (or pre-checking the account output) before collapsing every non-zero exit into `GhError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/upstream_gh.py:41 (`ensure_ready`)

chunk_findings.detail:
`Consent.consume` is a non-atomic check-then-set:

```python
if self.used:
    return False
self.used = True
return True
```

and `send_gh` reads `used` once in `_refusal` near the top, then does `write_report` and `gh.ensure_ready` (both of which can block on I/O and release the GIL), and only then calls `consent.consume()`. So the window between "consent looks unused" and "consent is marked used" spans network/disk work, and the mark itself is racy. Two concurrent `send_gh(root, bundle, repo, consent)` calls with the same `Consent` both pass `_refusal` (both see `used == False`), both reach `consume()`, and — because a CPython thread switch can occur between `LOAD_ATTR used`/`POP_JUMP_IF_TRUE` and `STORE_ATTR used` — both can observe `used == False` and both return `True`. Both then call `gh.create_issue`, producing two upstream issues from one consent. That directly contradicts the module's stated invariant ("not already used", "one consent, one submission") and the `ConsentLike.consume` contract of "single use". The provided `Consent` is the only concrete implementation in this file, so any caller passing it (rather than a separate race-safe minter object) is exposed. A minimal fix is to make the transition atomic (e.g. `if self.used: return False; self.used = True` guarded by a `threading.Lock`, or a compare-and-swap), or to consume the consent before the blocking work so the loser bails out immediately rather than after the I/O.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upstream_delivery.py — `Consent.consume` / `send_gh`

chunk_findings.detail: The test named/documented as verifying the "< 8 KB" acceptance does not compare against 8 KB at all; it compares the longest generated URL to the implementation's own constant `D.URL_MAX`. Since `issue_url` returns `None` exactly when the length exceeds `D.URL_MAX` (that is what `test_oversize_url_falls_back_to_the_file_and_says_so` relies on), the check reduces to "no real corpus URL hit the fallback." The only independent bound on `D.URL_MAX` comes from the oversize test, whose fixture (`"é"*900` expected + `"é"*3000` stderr, ~24–25 K characters once percent-encoded as `%C3%A9`) forces `URL_MAX < ~25000`. So an implementation with, say, `URL_MAX = 16000` (or even `12000`) passes both tests while emitting URLs far above the required 8 KB — the acceptance "URL < 8 KB for the whole real-text corpus" is never actually asserted. If the intent is to pin the 8 KB contract, the assertion needs a literal bound (e.g. `assert biggest < 8192`) rather than the production constant; as written the test cannot fail for a non-compliant threshold in the range `(max_corpus_url, ~25000)`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_upstream_delivery.py::test_url_under_8kb_for_the_whole_real_text_corpus (`assert biggest < D.URL_MAX`)

chunk_findings.detail: `ensure_ready` decides "logged in?" by running `gh auth status` through `_ask`, and `_ask` maps `ForgeError` to `GhError` and only `ForgeUnavailable` to `Unavailable`. But `gh auth status` signals "not logged into any GitHub hosts" with a *non-zero exit code* (it is not a missing-binary condition), so with `gh` installed but not authenticated `_check` produces a `ForgeError` and `ensure_ready` raises `GhError`, not `Unavailable`. That contradicts both this module's own docstring ("`gh` missing or not logged in is `Unavailable` with the reason") and the `Unavailable` docstring ("missing, not logged in, offline"), and it breaks the `gh absent/not-logged-in -> unavailable` acceptance path: the caller will surface a "gh said no" CLI error for an operator who simply has no login, and the stored reason will be gh's auth-status text rather than an unavailability verdict. The input that demonstrates it is a host with `gh` on PATH and no valid token: `gh auth status` exits 1, `_check` raises `ForgeError`, and `ensure_ready` raises `GhError` instead of `Unavailable`. (Verified only against the mapping implied by the imported `ForgeError`/`ForgeUnavailable` and `_check`; if `_check` special-cases this exit code, the finding does not apply.)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/upstream_gh.py ensure_ready

chunk_findings.detail:
The module docstring asserts the consent is "DEFINED here and MINTED elsewhere … nothing in this module can create one", and the intent requires that consent be unforgeable by the agent ("an agent-supplied flag alone is refused"; "never one the agent can construct"). But the very same file defines a plain, fully constructible `@dataclass Consent` (digest/expires_at/used + `consume`) with no secret, nonce, signature, or private constructor, and `send_gh` accepts any `ConsentLike`. The only guard is `_refusal`, which merely reads the caller-supplied attributes and compares `consent.digest == bundle.digest`. So an agent that can call `send_gh` can simply build the "consent" itself:

    Consent(digest=bundle.digest, expires_at=time.time() + 3600)

This passes every check (`digest` matches, `used` is False, not expired), `consume()` returns True, and `gh.create_issue` is invoked and the report is posted — with no operator interaction at all. The stated single-use/expiry/binding checks are therefore enforcement of fields the caller chooses, not of operator consent, which is exactly the property B-upstream-consent is supposed to guarantee. Either the constructible `Consent` must be removed/abstracted (so only the minter's authenticated type can satisfy the protocol), or `send_gh` must require the authenticated consent type rather than a structural `ConsentLike`.
